narrative:
The 2020 Los Angeles Angels entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season with genuine optimism — a revamped roster featuring Anthony Rendon's addition alongside Mike Trout and Shohei Ohtani promised something special. But the early weeks told a different story, as the Angels stumbled out of the gate in July, going just 2-6 and watching their bullpen surrender crucial leads. The pitching staff, anchored by a bloated 5.09 ERA, repeatedly undermined whatever offensive promise the lineup showed.

August became a tale of two halves within a single month. The Angels found moments of genuine brilliance — Tommy La Stella's walk-off two-run homer on August 17th was the season's single most impactful positive play, a swing that encapsulated what this offense could be at its best. Albert Pujols added a grand slam, and even backup catcher Jason Castro emerged as an unlikely hero. The Angels went 10-18 in August, a losing record, yet the competitive spirit never fully died as the offense kept punching back against tough opponents.

September represented the Angels' best baseball of the year, a 14-10 surge that came agonizingly too late to matter in the playoff race. The month opened with wild, high-leverage games against Houston — Jo Adell delivered a clutch two-run single in his debut season, and Anthony Rendon launched a pivotal three-run homer to swing a game decisively. Jared Walsh announced himself as a legitimate power threat, and even backup Anthony Bemboom contributed a memorable blast. The Angels were finally playing their best baseball, but the deficit from July's disastrous start proved insurmountable.

In the end, the 2020 Angels finished 26-34, missing the expanded playoff field and leaving the fanbase to wonder what might have been. With Trout, Ohtani, and Rendon all in the fold, the talent was undeniable — but a patchwork rotation and an unreliable bullpen, capable of surrendering game-defining homers at the worst moments, kept this team from reaching its potential. The September surge was a promise of better days ahead rather than a reward for the season just played.

chapters.title: Stumbling Out of the Gate
chapters.description: The Angels open the shortened season with a dismal 2-6 July, with the bullpen surrendering key homers and early promise quickly fading.

chapters.title: Chaos and Heart in August
chapters.description: August brings a rollercoaster of crushing blown leads and stunning offensive moments, with La Stella's walk-off homer serving as the emotional peak of a losing month.

chapters.title: Too Little, Too Late
chapters.description: September sees the Angels finally play their best baseball at 14-10, with Rendon, Walsh, Adell, and Pujols delivering clutch moments in a playoff push that arrives too late.
